description:
Wider opportunities to meet a spouse do not remove the need for wise discernment. Wesam Saad concludes the Courtship to Marriage course by applying its principles to social media, distance, conferences and connections between churches. He first reviews purity, responsible involvement and the assessment of faith and readiness. A fortunate outcome from an earlier relationship is not, in his argument, a reason to disregard those concerns when guiding the next generation. Addressing 1 Corinthians 7:9, he distinguishes sexual desire as a reason to consider marriage from the broader purpose he has described: serving God’s kingdom within the responsibilities of a household.

The practical discussion allows online services as tools while retaining accountable communication and careful enquiries. Long-distance contact should not reduce assessment to what someone says about theology; Saad stresses observing life and hearing from reliable people who know the person. He suggests visits, hospitality and cooperation between church leaders, with arrangements adjusted to the circumstances and the strength of existing relationships. At conferences, worship and spiritual growth remain the primary purpose, even where a desire to marry is present. The closing advice favours transparent introductions and respectful contact with families and churches, so that wider opportunities are pursued with dignity rather than secrecy or a hidden agenda.

questions.question: Why does Saad say a good outcome in an earlier marriage does not settle which approach is wise?
questions.answer: He uses a rescue illustration to distinguish receiving mercy after a risky course from establishing that course as a sound model. His concern is to help the next generation begin well. The percentages in the illustration are rhetorical, not evidence of a measured marriage success rate.

questions.question: How does the teacher understand the role of desire in 1 Corinthians 7:9?
questions.answer: Saad accepts that burning with passion can prompt someone to consider marriage. He distinguishes that prompt from making personal sexual satisfaction the whole purpose. In his explanation, marriage provides a household context for serving God, caring for a spouse and raising children in the knowledge of Christ.

questions.question: What concern governs his advice about private social-media communication?
questions.answer: He is concerned that extended private contact can develop attachment and compromise purity before a clear commitment exists. He therefore favours accountable group communication and supervision. He does not say that men and women cannot be friends, but questions unguarded private interaction under that description.

questions.question: Does the session reject all use of online services to meet a spouse?
questions.answer: No. Saad allows them as tools if the same principles are maintained. He suggests making intentions clear and directing enquiries through a parent or guardian. He expressly distinguishes these proposed arrangements from biblical principles and acknowledges that unfamiliar churches and distance make reliable assessment more difficult.

questions.question: What does he recommend when distance prevents ordinary observation of the other person?
questions.answer: Saad suggests visits, hospitality with church members and involvement from trusted believers so that there can be first-hand knowledge of the person’s life. He allows the arrangements to vary, including greater reliance on a well-known church with credible witnesses. Distance should not make important questions disappear.

questions.question: Why is discussing theology alone insufficient to assess a prospective spouse?
questions.answer: The teacher distinguishes correct answers from a life that reflects genuine faith and readiness. Group Bible discussion can help establish beliefs, but he also wants evidence of conduct and responses to real situations. The person being considered is more than a collection of doctrinal statements.

questions.question: What should remain primary when attending a conference?
questions.answer: Saad says worship, receiving God’s word and spiritual edification should remain the main purpose. A desire to marry can be present and appropriate group conversation may create opportunities. He warns against pretending to attend for worship while making the search for a spouse a hidden primary agenda.

questions.question: How can contact between church leaders help with introductions?
questions.answer: He suggests discussing intentions with one’s elders, who can contact another church and ask about appropriate introductions and family involvement. Transparent arrangements allow people to expect the visitor and understand the purpose. Saad offers several possible channels rather than requiring a single procedure or the pastor personally in every case.
